title: PF Withdrawal Rules – A Comprehensive Guide to Rules, Documents Required, and Types
summary: EPF withdrawal rules since 29 June 2026: when you can take part or all of your PF, what you need to claim, how long it takes and when it is taxed.
body_markdown:
Since 29 June 2026, withdrawals from your PF (the Employees' Provident Fund, or EPF) follow the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026. It was made under the Code on Social Security, 2020, and published in the Gazette of India that day as G.S.R. 525(E). It replaced the 1952 scheme. Existing members moved into it automatically.


Under it, you can take part of your balance while working, for illness, education, marriage or a home, once you have 12 months' membership. You must keep a minimum balance. You can take all of it when you retire after 55, or after 12 months without a job covered by EPF. This guide covers what you need to claim, the rules, the time it takes and the tax.


## What do you need to withdraw PF?


You need an activated UAN (Universal Account Number). It is the identity number that EPFO, the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation, gives you for life. Your Aadhaar and bank account must be linked to it, and your KYC (Know Your Customer) details approved.


EPFO's older FAQ describes the same condition. For claims without employer attestation, the UAN must be active and at least the bank account and Aadhaar KYC approved.


Here is the short list:


- An active UAN.
- Aadhaar linked to it and approved.
- A bank account linked to it and approved.
- Your PAN (Permanent Account Number, your income-tax ID), so that any TDS is cut at the normal rate and not the higher one. TDS is tax deducted before the money reaches you.
- Form 121, a written declaration that your tax for the year will be nil, which replaced Forms 15G and 15H. You need it only if that applies to you (see the tax section below).


You claim online, on EPFO's member portal or the UMANG app. Since April 2025 you no longer upload a cheque leaf or an attested passbook image for an online claim. The employer's approval for linking your bank account to the UAN has also been removed. Both changes come from a government press release (PIB, 3 April 2025).


## When can you withdraw PF?


Since 29 June 2026, withdrawals follow the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026, which replaced the 1952 scheme. The rule that applies depends on whether you are still working and what the money is for.


A partial withdrawal is a part of your balance taken while the account stays open. Its upper limit is your eligible balance. That is what stands to your credit after you keep back a minimum balance. The minimum balance is 25% of everything paid in for you (your share and your employer's) plus interest, measured up to the date of withdrawal.


Ground How much Membership needed How often


Illness of you or family members Up to 100% of the eligible balance 12 months No count stated


Education of you or family members Up to 100% of the eligible balance 12 months Not more than ten times in your membership


Marriage of you or family members Up to 100% of the eligible balance 12 months Not more than five times in your membership


Housing: buying a flat, house or site, building, repaying a home loan for these, additions, alterations or renovation Up to 100% of the eligible balance 12 months Not more than five times in your membership


"Special circumstances", the scheme's own term Up to 100% of the eligible balance 12 months Not more than two times in a financial year


Full withdrawal: retirement after 55, permanent and total incapacity, moving abroad for good, retrenchment, voluntary retirement scheme The whole balance No membership period stated Not applicable


Full withdrawal: simply leaving a job The whole balance 12 months without covered work Not applicable


Each partial withdrawal must be at least ₹1,000. Your membership counts earlier service and earlier membership, unless you withdrew your balance in between.


What changed from the 1952 scheme? Purpose-wise limits, such as 90% for a house, do not appear in the 2026 scheme. One minimum-balance rule applies to every ground. And the counts in the table started afresh for every member on 29 June 2026.


Some older pages, EPFO's own scheme page among them, still print the 1952 rules, such as full withdrawal after two months of unemployment. For the 2026 scheme the waiting period for leaving a job is 12 months.


## Can you withdraw PF while you are still working?


Yes, for the grounds in the table, after 12 months' membership. You can take up to your eligible balance, which in practice is up to about 75% of your account.


Here is an illustration. Say you and your employer have put in ₹4,00,000 with interest. The minimum balance is 25%, so ₹1,00,000 must stay. Up to ₹3,00,000 is available. This assumes the account holds only contributions and their interest.


If you leave a job before 12 months' membership, you can still take up to your eligible balance.


The money is paid into your bank or post office account.


## Can you withdraw all of your PF after leaving a job or retiring?


You can take your whole balance on retirement after 55, or on permanent and total incapacity for work. You can also take it just before you migrate from India for good or for a job abroad, or on retrenchment. The same applies if your service ends under a voluntary retirement scheme.


Two narrow cases, certain transfers to establishments the Code does not cover and retrenchment with compensation, are paid only after two months.


If you simply resign, the rule is different. You can close the account only after 12 months in a row without a job covered by EPF. Women who resign to get married do not have to wait. Until the 12 months pass, you can make partial withdrawals for a ground in the table.


Take Ravi, 27, a sales executive in Visakhapatnam. He resigns after 3 years and 4 months with ₹1,90,000 in his EPF and takes a break before his next job. Resigning is not one of the cases above, so he can close the account only after 12 months without covered work. Until then he can make partial withdrawals for a ground in the table, keeping the 25% minimum balance.


Someone who withdraws everything and is employed again is treated as a fresh member.


If you are moving to a new job, a transfer is a different route from a withdrawal. Our guide to[moving and checking your EPF](https://koshex.com/blog/employee-provident-fund-your-key-to-a-more-secure-and-stable-future) covers it, and the[EPF calculator](https://koshex.com/calculators/epf-calculator) shows how a balance can grow.


### What happens to the balance if the member dies?


The balance goes to the nominee, the person named on the portal. Without a nominee it goes to family members in equal shares, and without them to the legal heir. The scheme says a member must make a fresh nomination after marriage.


## How do you claim PF online, and how long does it take?


You file the claim online, on EPFO's member portal or the UMANG app. EPFO's rule is to settle a complete claim within 20 days of receiving it. If the claim has a deficiency, EPFO must tell you within those 20 days.


For advance claims that pass EPFO's checks, EPFO raised the limit for automatic settlement from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh in June 2025. These cover illness, education, marriage and housing. They are processed without any human involvement (PIB, 24 June 2025).


A government press release said EPFO's auto mode brings settlement from up to 20 days to under three days (PIB, 12 February 2026).


A physical claim is needed only if online filing fails for a technical reason. It goes through your employer, who must forward it within five days. Payment is by electronic transfer to a bank or post office account.


If EPFO delays a complete claim without a good reason, the scheme makes it liable for penal interest at 12% a year.


## Is a PF withdrawal taxed?


Not if you have five years or more of continuous service, or your job ended for a reason outside your control. Otherwise yes, and TDS may be cut. The law is the Income-tax Act, 2025.


A withdrawal is tax-free in any of these cases:


- You have five years or more of continuous service with your employer.
- Your job ended through ill-health, the employer's closure or another cause beyond your control.
- The money moves to a new employer's PF or to NPS (the National Pension System).


Earlier jobs count towards the five years if their PF balance was transferred in.


Otherwise the tax is recalculated as if EPF had never been tax-free. The extra tax is payable in the year the balance becomes payable. The TDS is credited to you as tax paid.


### If you have five years or more of continuous service


The withdrawal is not taxed. No TDS applies, because TDS on EPF depends on the balance being taxable. Earlier employers' service counts where their balance was transferred into your current account.


### If you have less than five years


If none of the tax-free reasons applies, the balance is taxable. EPFO deducts 10% TDS when the payment is ₹50,000 or more and is taxable under the rule above. Without a PAN, TDS is cut at the highest of the rate in the Act, the rates in force or 20% (section 397).


Ravi's balance is ₹1,90,000 after 3 years and 4 months, and he resigned. He is under five years and resigning is not an exception, so the balance is taxable. The payment is above ₹50,000, so EPFO deducts 10%, which is ₹19,000, if he has given his PAN.


Form 121 can stop the TDS. A resident can give it only if the tax on the year's total income will be nil. If you are under 60, a second test applies too. The income you declare on Form 121 must be within the tax-free limit. At 60 or over, the first test alone applies. Ravi is under 60, so he needs both.


You can also apply for a lower or nil deduction certificate, on Form 128.


### If you move the money to a new employer or NPS


If you join a new employer and your balance moves to that employer's PF, nothing is taxed. Ravi's 3 years and 4 months would then count towards the five years. Moving the entire balance to NPS is also not taxed. Our article on[tax on EPF interest](https://koshex.com/blog/how-epf-interest-is-taxed) covers the interest you earn while the money stays in the account.


## What happens to your EPS pension money?


The pension part is separate from your EPF balance. It is the Employees' Pension Scheme, or EPS, and its rules decide what you get on leaving.


With at least ten years of eligible service, EPS pays a monthly pension from age 58. You can start it from 50, reduced by 4% for every year you are short of 58. Six months or more of service counts as a full year.


The monthly pension is pensionable wages multiplied by pensionable service, divided by 70. Pensionable wages are your average monthly wages over the 60 months before you leave, capped at the wage ceiling.


With less than ten years, you can take a one-time withdrawal benefit. If you leave before 58, you get it 36 months after your last contribution became due, or at 58 if that comes first. The alternative is to carry your service forward with a scheme certificate. The scheme sets the withdrawal amount from a table.


Ravi, with under ten years of service, could take the withdrawal benefit only 36 months after his last contribution, or keep a scheme certificate.


For how pension plans work more widely, see our guide to[annuities and pension plans](https://koshex.com/blog/nps-annuity-and-pension-plans) . For what retirees do with a lump sum, see[retirement income](https://koshex.com/blog/retirement-income) .
